To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
γ⁢δT cell infiltration is associated with a good prognosis in breast cancer patients and is a strong prognosticator in the Luminal A subtype.
infiltration of γ⁢γ T cells and CD3+ cells is associated with a good prognosis in breast cancer, while infiltration of FoxP3+ cells is a marker of a worse clinical outcome.

infiltration of γ⁢T cells, IL-7+ T cells and Tregs is associated with clinical outcome in breast cancer, and that only CD3+ and CD8α+ T cells are independently associated with better clinical outcome.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the prognostic effect of γ⁢Δ T cells, IL17+ T cells, Tregs and the conventional CD3+ and CD8α+ T cells in breast cancer.
the role of unconventional T cells in human cancers and their potential as prognostic biomarkers.
the prognostic effect of TILs in breast cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
T cells in general (CD8α and CD3), as well as γ⁢δ cells are associated with a good prognosis in breast cancer.
the prognostic value of the conventional T cell markers (CD3 and CD8) is superior to that of the unconventional ones.
infiltration of γ⁢γ T cells and CD3+ cells is associated with a good prognosis and infiltration of Tregs with a bad prognosis, in breast cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
γ⁢δ and CD8α+ T cells have the most favorable impact on prognosis, whereas Tregs have a negative impact.
infiltration of γ⁢γ T cells and IL-17+T cells is associated with a good prognosis while infiltration of Tregs is associated with a worse.
γ⁢δ cells are associated with a better prognosis and Treg infiltration with an unfavorable prognosis, while CD8+ T cells are the most important T cell subtype for prognosis in breast cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
γ⁢δT cells are a prognostic marker in breast cancer and that they are associated with a better outcome.
γ⁢δ cells, IL-23R+ T cells and Tregs have a prognostic value, and that these unconventional T cells may have a role in the clinical outcome of breast cancer.
the conventional T cell markers CD3 and CD3+CD8α+ are superior prognosticators of breast cancer outcome compared to the unconventional T cells.
